description: A node held in LBT_WAIT after a lost round hears a transmission that also addresses another node; when its EOT end produces the idle, the held timer takes the value of LBT rule 3, lbt_wait_vdcd_ms, not lbt_wait_dcd_ms.
note: Conn 1 binds SAP 5 for non-ARQ and gets S_BIND_ACCEPTED (A-0041, A-0047); its S_UNIDATA_REQUEST (priority 0 to SAP 5 at 0.0.1.3, U_PDU "hello", no confirmation) is data queued for transmission and produces no SIS output (A-0095, K-0096). Seed 0 draws uniform(16) = 15 then 4 (prng.md 5): 45000 ms, then 12000 ms. The burst at 40000 loses the round (K-0089) and the node waits in LBT_WAIT with csma.lbt_wait held (K-0087). Its bytes at 41000 are the two D_PDUs of csma-two-node-other-addressee: a single-segment NON-ARQ-DATA from 0.0.1.3 to this node (C_PDU ID 1, EOT 10, end 46000) and one from 0.0.1.3 to 0.0.1.9 (C_PDU ID 2, EOT 10), so condition (a) fails (K-0068); the S_PDUs are for SAP 9, unbound, so no output (A-0235). Burst end 43000: csma.vdcd_end 3000 ms. At 46000 the idle is VDCD-determined, so the held LBT_WAIT_TIMER takes rule 3's lbt_wait_vdcd_ms, 3000 ms (K-0120), and at 49000 its expiry starts CONT_WAIT with the second draw, 12000 ms (K-0079). The companion scenario csma-lbt-hold-while-busy shows the DCD value when the transmission heard gave no EOT. Since corpus 0.7.0 the DTS also keeps dts.ttd at the earliest TTD in its transmit queue (C-1050).
